instruction: Install the unpacked Chrome extension from the Desktop folder (helloExtension) and verify it appears in the extensions list.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get install unzip -y && unzip /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip -d /home/user/Desktop/ && rm /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip

metadata.explanation: This variation asks to install the extension and verify it by checking if 'Hello Extensions' appears in the installed extensions names list. Uses existing getters is_in_list metric and get_find_installed_extension_name getter.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is correct: 'get_find_installed_extension_name' reads Chrome Preferences file and extracts extension names from 'extensions.settings[id].manifest.name', which is the correct location for installed extension metadata
Metric logic is correct: 'is_in_list' performs membership checking (expected in result list), which properly verifies if the extension name appears in the installed extensions list
Data flow is semantically correct: getter returns list of extension names -> metric checks if 'Hello Extensions' is in that list
Complete coverage: instruction requires 'verify it appears in the extensions list', evaluator checks exactly this requirement
Expected value is semantically reasonable: 'Hello Extensions' is expected to match the extension's manifest.json name field (assumed verified by task creator)
Postconfig includes 0.5s sleep which allows Chrome to persist extension data to Preferences file
No UI dependency: getter reads from file system (Preferences file), not from UI state, so the heuristic warning about UI/postconfig is not applicable here
